A missing/incompatible runtime cannot be replaced by remembered workflow instructions.

requirements.group: Skills, guides, packaging, and phase implementation boundaries
requirements.title: Separate operator instructions from managed-role prompts
requirements.behavior: The Discovery host may perform the investigation through public commands. Consensus/Audit operator guides tell the host how to prepare, invoke, inspect, and present their managed phase; internal semantic-role prompts are not an invitation for the host to duplicate or replace that phase’s result.
requirements.enforcement: Keep phase-owned operator guides and role prompts separately versioned within the same release. Provide only relevant instructions to each role. Preserve returned artifacts rather than rewriting a failed reconciliation in the parent conversation.
acceptance_criteria: A host invoking Consensus does not also supply its preferred diagnosis or perform an unrecorded replacement synthesis.
A role receives its required semantic instructions without unrelated phase workflows or peer private state.

requirements.group: Skills, guides, packaging, and phase implementation boundaries
requirements.title: Install and update without damaging the user’s environment
requirements.behavior: One release SHALL install the executable and selected host skill collection without modifying target repositories, unrelated skills, or global host preferences. Reinstallation is idempotent for owned unchanged files; modified/conflicting files receive a diagnostic or explicit replacement choice. Resolve command identity before use.
requirements.enforcement: Track installation-owned resources and runtime identity; detect collisions and stale wrappers. Test from a separate installation prefix with source access removed. No Python/uv or marketplace dependency is required for the core executable.
acceptance_criteria: Repeated install/update/remove preserves an unrelated sentinel skill and user modifications.
An earlier conflicting executable on PATH cannot silently receive Orchestrate operations.

requirements.group: Skills, guides, packaging, and phase implementation boundaries
requirements.title: Use public contracts instead of phase internals
requirements.behavior: Phase implementations SHALL consume upstream finalized public contracts, not another phase’s private database, application services, or unfinished state. Rust crate boundaries are the preferred enforcement mechanism. Contract consumers must work without initializing the producer runtime.
requirements.enforcement: Use explicit allowed dependencies, private implementation modules, narrow contract surfaces, and dependency-policy tests. A contract module is not permission to expose the entire producer domain model.
acceptance_criteria: A forbidden internal import fails; the public contract consumer still compiles and functions.
Removing an upstream working database does not break downstream work when required public artifacts remain.

requirements.group: Skills, guides, packaging, and phase implementation boundaries
requirements.title: Share mechanics only when the behavior is genuinely common
requirements.behavior: Hashing, file publication, identity, bounded execution, and provider transport may be shared. Discovery judgment, consensus endorsement, and Audit conformance SHALL not be forced into a universal semantic graph or shared scoring engine. Crate organization does not by itself prevent runtime access or an unauthorized dependency change.
requirements.enforcement: Test dependency declarations, aliases, features, and re-exports; independently validate shared encoding and path behavior against fixed vectors. Keep phase policies and permission checks at their real boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: A forbidden Cargo dependency edge is detected even if someone makes the formerly forbidden import public.
An intentionally broken shared digest/path helper fails independent consumer vectors instead of passing shared round-trip tests.

requirements.group: Verification and delivery acceptance
requirements.title: Test machinery through real public boundaries
requirements.behavior: The suite SHALL combine deterministic rule tests with real-CLI integration/E2E using actual files, Git data, subprocesses, parsing, persistence, finalization, and restart. Scripted agents/providers control behavior but may not write accepted artifacts or bypass production validators/finalizers.
requirements.enforcement: Use both focused controlled adapters and a protocol-level subprocess emulator. The scripted Discovery investigator performs the same public operations as a host. The initial complete journey uses external Build registration.
acceptance_criteria: A known-good scripted journey crosses all real stage boundaries.
A malformed or malicious scripted result fails the real parser/publication path rather than being pre-rejected solely inside a mock.

requirements.group: Verification and delivery acceptance
requirements.title: Give every critical guarantee an adversarial test
requirements.behavior: Acceptance SHALL trace each required behavior to positive and negative cases at its enforcement boundary, including meaningful interruption, concurrency, or boundary cases. High line coverage or an impressive test count is not a substitute.
requirements.enforcement: Maintain requirement-to-case mapping and execution status. Use independent expected values, fault injection, generated state sequences, and selected mutations of critical guards. No mandatory case may disappear by filtering or silently skipping it.
acceptance_criteria: Disabling artifact verification, accepting drafts, unioning supporters, or using moving HEAD causes a test failure.
The report identifies planned, passed, failed, blocked, unsupported, and not-run cases separately.

requirements.group: Verification and delivery acceptance
requirements.title: Isolate test infrastructure from real work and answer keys
requirements.behavior: Automated trials SHALL use disposable roots, synthetic repositories/data, child-local environment settings, and examiner-only answer keys. Offline tests have no model credentials/network. Live tests are explicitly authorized, bounded, and use only the selected provider’s required credentials.
requirements.enforcement: The harness cannot write the real orchestration store, source projects, or installed user skills. Validate known-good and faulty reference implementations independently before using them as grading oracles.
acceptance_criteria: Offline lanes fail loudly if a provider invocation or external request is attempted.
The agent cannot receive hidden solutions through source history, sibling artifacts, test configuration, or grading keys within its declared boundary.

requirements.group: Verification and delivery acceptance
requirements.title: Qualify installed hosts, not just prompt text
requirements.behavior: Low-strength live E2E smoke tests SHALL exercise the actual installed skill and executable in each host/surface claimed supported. Record the host version, requested/observed model profile, guide loading, actual public operations, result, and stopping behavior. Manual graphical-host checks are labeled manual.
requirements.enforcement: Use fresh actual host sessions and explicit skills. Pasting SKILL.md into a model prompt, or testing a CLI instead of an editor surface, does not qualify the untested installation path.
acceptance_criteria: The supported Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor surfaces actually discover the phase skills and load the correct guide.
A skipped live test or unavailable credential is reported blocked, not counted as host compatibility.

requirements.group: Verification and delivery acceptance
requirements.title: Test semantic fidelity against independent rubrics
requirements.behavior: Live semantic evaluations SHALL judge Discovery usefulness, Consensus fidelity, and Audit correctness using original inputs and independently authored expected behaviors. Cheap-model smoke success does not qualify another profile’s reasoning. Retain every trial and allowed retry; do not rerun until a preferred result appears.
requirements.enforcement: Use curated positive/negative fixtures, permitted alternatives, and predeclared repetitions. The initial small qualification corpus runs five fresh trials per selected scenario/profile; this is a diagnostic minimum, not a statistical reliability claim. LLM graders may assist only after their own controls are validated.
acceptance_criteria: Known-good and known-bad semantic outputs are discriminated by the grading rubric.
Order/wording/condition perturbations cannot be excused by accepting the model’s own extracted account as the answer key.

requirements.group: Verification and delivery acceptance
requirements.title: Report qualification honestly on real target environments
requirements.behavior: Initial delivery SHALL be qualified natively on the user’s macOS environment. Linux or Windows support, enforced access isolation, multi-assessor Audit, and parallel model dispatch are qualified only if shipped and claimed. Rust compilation or Linux CI alone is not evidence of native Mac behavior.
requirements.enforcement: Publish a support/capability matrix with actual execution records and limits. All core machinery cases and selected must-pass semantic fixtures must run; no observed critical false acceptance, integrity failure, or claimed-isolation breach may remain in the accepted qualification set.
acceptance_criteria: Native path/process/cancellation cases pass without a hidden platform workaround.
Unexecuted hosts, optional capabilities, and deferred internal Build appear explicitly outside the qualified result.

acceptance_cases.setup: Invoke help, version, guide, inspect, or status on a fresh test installation without credentials.
acceptance_cases.expected: The documented read-only operation works or reports a missing local artifact clearly; no model launch, run creation, repo edit, or credential requirement is introduced.

acceptance_cases.setup: Supply an unknown phase or omit a mandatory explicit phase.
acceptance_cases.expected: A specific input error; no inferred phase, model invocation, or partial mutation.

acceptance_cases.setup: Complete Discovery, then leave the process idle; repeat for Consensus and Audit.
acceptance_cases.expected: No successor phase, extra model session, or implementation action is launched. Compare actual invocation logs and directories, not the final prose.

acceptance_cases.setup: Try a phase with a parent of the wrong type, a draft parent, or a different effort's parent.
acceptance_cases.expected: The contract mismatch is rejected before semantic execution; no child is falsely finalized.

acceptance_cases.setup: Install packaged binary and skills into a disposable prefix; remove access to the source checkout.
acceptance_cases.expected: All supported guides and necessary resources load from the installation. No source-tree or old Python/uv fallback is required.

acceptance_cases.setup: Install twice, update, and remove the test installation beside an unrelated sentinel skill.
acceptance_cases.expected: Orchestrate's managed files behave idempotently under the installer policy; unrelated skills/configuration remain unchanged. Installed modifications are not silently destroyed.

acceptance_cases.setup: Put a conflicting executable earlier on PATH or make the intended runtime absent.
acceptance_cases.expected: The wrapper identifies the selected executable/version or stops with a useful mismatch diagnostic; it does not operate a remembered workflow against the wrong program.

acceptance_cases.setup: Inspect each generated phase wrapper and host metadata; include Build before Build is implemented.
acceptance_cases.expected: Fixed phase-to-guide mapping with no classifier. Canonical semantic bodies are not independently duplicated. Discovery, Consensus, and Audit skills are installed; internal Build execution/skill is not advertised. External implementation registration remains available.

acceptance_cases.setup: In a fresh actual Codex/Claude/Cursor session, explicitly invoke an installed phase skill.
acceptance_cases.expected: The host discovers that skill, loads the matching guide, and uses the intended executable. Record host version and evidence; pasting the skill into a prompt is not this test.

acceptance_cases.setup: Send a vague request without invoking an explicit-only phase skill, then explicitly invoke it with missing inputs.
acceptance_cases.expected: The implicit-invocation policy behaves as configured; the explicit invocation produces a prerequisite diagnostic rather than choosing another phase. Grade host invocation separately from general chat behavior.

acceptance_cases.setup: Invoke Consensus explicitly but include user text requesting investigation or code edits outside Consensus.
acceptance_cases.expected: The active workflow does not silently become Discovery or Build. Necessary disagreement is surfaced without running the other phase.

acceptance_cases.setup: Begin a resumable run, change installed guide/runtime identity, and resume in a fresh session.
acceptance_cases.expected: Record runtime/guide/policy identities. An incompatible resume stops without data mutation; a specifically supported compatible continuation is explicit and recorded. Never silently load current rules as though they governed the older run.

acceptance_cases.setup: Two unrelated repositories share the basename `server`; both use `TIX-1234`.
acceptance_cases.expected: Their records cannot collide or cross-link. Display names are not the sole identity.

acceptance_cases.setup: One repository has two requests with similar slugs and several runs per phase.
acceptance_cases.expected: Explicit effort/run selection targets the intended records; “latest directory” never silently chooses unrelated authority.

acceptance_cases.setup: Use spaces, Unicode, separators, `..`, absolute path fragments, and unusually long slugs.
acceptance_cases.expected: Valid labels round-trip; invalid labels receive a clear error; no escape from the configured storage root or accidental overwrite. Test actual supported filesystem rules.

acceptance_cases.setup: Refer to the same repository through a symlink and canonical path; test macOS `/var` and `/private/var`.
acceptance_cases.expected: The documented alias policy is consistent; path spelling alone does not merge unrelated repos or cause false containment failures.

acceptance_cases.setup: Prepopulate tracked/untracked files, `.gitignore`, and local Git exclude/configuration; run Discovery, Consensus, and Audit.
acceptance_cases.expected: Product-file bytes and configuration remain unchanged. Any claimed zero-repository-write guarantee includes relevant Git administration effects, not only a clean diff.

acceptance_cases.setup: Use an explicit test orchestration root and invoke from a different working directory.
acceptance_cases.expected: Paths resolve according to the documented CLI contract; no writes leak into the real home, the caller's cwd, or target repository.

acceptance_cases.setup: Two processes create runs simultaneously for the same effort.
acceptance_cases.expected: Unique run identities; no shared output collision; each result remains attributable. Parallel model execution is optional, but concurrent local commands cannot corrupt records.

acceptance_cases.setup: Move an artifact bundle to another allowed location, or make the original source path unavailable.
acceptance_cases.expected: Self-contained public content and retained lineage remain inspectable; unavailable external references are reported, not guessed. Relocating labels does not create another opinion.

acceptance_cases.setup: Make the root unwritable or simulate allocation/write failure.
acceptance_cases.expected: A normal diagnostic and no fabricated finalized artifact. The application does not invent a different storage root to bypass the failure.

acceptance_cases.setup: Create commit A, initialize a comparison cohort, then advance the original checkout to B before the second Discovery.
acceptance_cases.expected: All cohort investigations use A unless a new baseline/cohort is explicitly selected. The manifest records the material actually supplied.

acceptance_cases.setup: At A, add dirty tracked edits and untracked repro files, then start a committed-baseline investigation.
acceptance_cases.expected: The investigation sees committed A, not the dirty version. Original dirty/untracked work is neither cleaned nor overwritten.

acceptance_cases.setup: Combine finalized opinions from different source commits, requests, or incorporated constraints.
acceptance_cases.expected: The mismatch is detected before claiming direct comparability. No automatic mixing as three equivalent votes. Any future comparison-across-baselines mode needs its own explicit contract.

acceptance_cases.setup: Change an upstream request after one run, retaining the same human slug.
acceptance_cases.expected: Request identity changes are visible; older opinions do not silently become opinions about the new request.

acceptance_cases.setup: Change the source during snapshot preparation.
acceptance_cases.expected: The supplied committed snapshot is consistent with its recorded identity, or preparation fails. No mixed snapshot labeled as one commit.

acceptance_cases.setup: Investigate a repo without a commit, or a target that is not supported by the committed-snapshot implementation.
acceptance_cases.expected: A clear unsupported/prerequisite result. The program does not invent a commit, make an initial commit, or silently switch to dirty-tree semantics.

acceptance_cases.setup: Include executable modes, supported symlinks, binary files, and unsupported submodule/LFS arrangements.
acceptance_cases.expected: The declared snapshot policy preserves relevant supported inputs and explicitly handles unsupported ones; no silent omission of required source material.

acceptance_cases.setup: Place a known solution on an extra branch or in a cache not authorized for the investigator.
acceptance_cases.expected: That solution is not reachable through the provided research boundary. Check refs/config/caches actually exposed; do not equate a separate directory with isolation.

acceptance_cases.setup: Run A creates a distinctive repro, notes, and a false recommendation. Start B from the same cohort.
acceptance_cases.expected: A's generated material is absent from the original source and B's supplied workspace/packet. B receives its own run state only.

acceptance_cases.setup: Plant different sentinels in peer outputs, examiner keys, original dirty files, and unrelated home files; inspect actual outgoing packets/tool results.
acceptance_cases.expected: No forbidden sentinel is supplied to the semantic role. Separately assert useful authorized source remains available; “empty input” is not a passing isolation solution.

acceptance_cases.setup: **Conditional: enforced peer access.** An adversarial probe attempts a direct read of the known peer path using the investigator's actual capabilities.
acceptance_cases.expected: Access is denied by the declared boundary. If only cooperative policy exists, this capability is NOT QUALIFIED; an unquoted sentinel or a verbal refusal is insufficient.

acceptance_cases.setup: **Conditional: enforced peer access.** Repeat peer access through symlink/relative traversal, process execution, relevant Git metadata, and allowed retrieval tools.
acceptance_cases.expected: No alternate authorized tool bypasses the claimed restriction. A filesystem-only result does not qualify browser/connectors or an unrestricted shell.

acceptance_cases.setup: Run a successful, failing, and interrupted experiment producing files and temporary service data.
acceptance_cases.expected: Application-owned check/reproduction effects use only declared run-owned disposable resources; target repository is unchanged; receipts distinguish experiment patches from the original target. Stronger arbitrary-process confinement is claimed only under a qualified boundary.

acceptance_cases.setup: Start two run-owned experiments with similarly named files, ports, and output paths.
acceptance_cases.expected: Separate resource identities; no shared writable caches/data cause cross-run evidence or result contamination. If parallel execution is unsupported, reject safely without corruption.

acceptance_cases.setup: Attempt cleanup with a sibling-run path, a symlink to the target repo, and a stale ownership marker.
acceptance_cases.expected: Cleanup refuses unowned/unsafe resources; it does not delete the source, peer evidence, or unrelated test sentinels.

acceptance_cases.setup: Run normal low-strength Discovery with misleading sibling artifacts present outside its permitted input.
acceptance_cases.expected: No incorporation or citation of peer material; record observed behavior separately from enforcement qualification. Use an independent trace/input audit, not only text matching.

acceptance_cases.setup: Give a small solvable request with explicit repository evidence and acceptance behavior.
acceptance_cases.expected: The scripted path can finalize through public operations; live Discovery produces an actionable opinion rather than only a completed ledger.

acceptance_cases.setup: Omit a required research/check item; try to finalize.
acceptance_cases.expected: The missing obligation remains visible and finalization follows the declared gate. The model cannot clear it by renaming an unrelated record.

acceptance_cases.setup: Record a required source as unavailable, a nonapplicable check with a reason, and an unresolved product decision.
acceptance_cases.expected: These are distinct from successful verification. Blockers are preserved; legitimate scope-limited outcomes remain possible where policy allows them.

acceptance_cases.setup: research establishes that no implementation change is necessary.
acceptance_cases.expected: Research can be dispositioned without a fabricated requirement/task. A justified preservation requirement is still allowed when genuinely needed.

acceptance_cases.setup: Revise a premise or invalidate an assumption after the draft was reviewed.
acceptance_cases.expected: Dependent conclusions/review status become stale as specified; unrelated valid evidence remains reusable. No silent finalization on old support.

acceptance_cases.setup: Add contrary evidence to a previously supported conclusion.
acceptance_cases.expected: The evidence remains represented and the affected decision cannot silently keep an unqualified old status. Live assessment handles its meaning instead of counting supporters.

acceptance_cases.setup: A reproduction demonstrates a defect, but no repair has been executed; another command exits zero without meaningful assertions.
acceptance_cases.expected: Receipts report observations, not proof of a repair. The final opinion distinguishes reproduced failure, proposed solution, and actual validation.

acceptance_cases.setup: The ticket incorrectly describes existing code; a separate product rule genuinely is unavailable.
acceptance_cases.expected: Discovery can correct the mistaken premise while asking for the missing product authority; it must not ask the user to choose an ordinary delegated technical detail.

acceptance_cases.setup: Interrupt a run with saved findings, then resume from a fresh caller/session.
acceptance_cases.expected: Saved work is recovered; identities and unresolved state remain honest. No duplicate replacement run merely to bypass a blocker.

acceptance_cases.setup: one investigator-owned run emits several files/copies and changes sessions.
acceptance_cases.expected: One investigator-owned run remains one logical opinion across sessions/files/exports. No nested investigator committee is required by the initial product.

acceptance_cases.setup: Three opinions endorse the same actionable behavior in different wording.
acceptance_cases.expected: The Agreement preserves the behavior and correct support. Terminology changes alone do not create disagreement.

acceptance_cases.setup: Two opinions endorse a repair; the third explicitly disagrees.
acceptance_cases.expected: A coherent majority result is possible under the chosen policy, with dissent visible. Do not collapse every 2–1 result into an inconclusive shrug.

acceptance_cases.setup: Two endorse X; the third is silent. Compare with a third that contradicts X.
acceptance_cases.expected: Support/contradiction/not-observed remain distinct; silence is not a negative vote or an endorsement.

acceptance_cases.setup: X is supported by A/B; Y by B/C; the requested package requires both.
acceptance_cases.expected: Per-claim majorities remain visible but no common-majority endorsement of X+Y is asserted. Independently calculate supporter-set intersection.

acceptance_cases.setup: All agree on “X only when P”; the candidate omits P.
acceptance_cases.expected: Structural reference/condition rules reject a detected omission; live grading checks that meaning was not broadened. Do not claim the validator understands arbitrary prose.

acceptance_cases.setup: One opinion adds attractive feature Z; model places Z in an extra recommendation paragraph outside adopted claims.
acceptance_cases.expected: Output binding disallows unaccounted mandatory instructions; semantic grading checks that paraphrases do not sneak Z into the Agreement.

acceptance_cases.setup: A majority rejects “replace interface”; model marks that rejected proposal decisive.
acceptance_cases.expected: The adopted direction is represented as the supported scoped alternative, such as retain the interface, rather than a rejected positive claim.

acceptance_cases.setup: Supply the same run through two aliases/copies; or alter its metadata but retain the same original run identity.
acceptance_cases.expected: One logical opinion is counted. Conflicting copies of one identity are reported, not counted as independent voters. Equal text alone is not proof that two genuinely distinct runs are aliases.

acceptance_cases.setup: One of the expected three opinions fails or is unavailable.
acceptance_cases.expected: Expected participation stays 3. A user-requested partial comparison may report findings, but no Agreement is adoptable until three eligible slots are complete. Replacement is explicit and retained.

acceptance_cases.setup: All three opinions overlook an explicit user requirement.
acceptance_cases.expected: The request remains bound to the effort; the Agreement does not gain authority to delete the requirement by omission. Semantic grading checks preservation; automated claims are limited to representable constraints.

acceptance_cases.setup: No actionable package obtains required support, but useful shared findings exist.
acceptance_cases.expected: Publish an honest comparison with the missing decision; no fabricated build-ready Agreement and no empty diagnostic pretending comparison never happened.

acceptance_cases.setup: Permute input order and change neutral provider labels without changing the opinions.
acceptance_cases.expected: Mechanical counts/eligibility are invariant. Live quality checks prohibit provider prestige, ordering, and verbosity from manufacturing support.

acceptance_cases.setup: One report has a concrete counterexample to a majority premise.
acceptance_cases.expected: Dissent is retained and qualified rather than erased. Consensus still reports endorsement counts honestly; it does not invent additional research or new votes.

acceptance_cases.setup: Complete reconciliation, then mutate an input before publication/consumption; delete an unneeded upstream private database.
acceptance_cases.expected: Verify public input identities at intake and verify retained authoritative bytes before publication/consumption. Tampering with those bytes fails. A live original path changing after correct capture does not retarget the frozen input. Private upstream databases are unnecessary.

acceptance_cases.setup: Include internal ledgers and summaries in retained storage but exclude them from the declared consensus input projection.
acceptance_cases.expected: Models receive the substantive finalized opinion and approved context, not an accidental recursive dump of the entire run. Retention is not automatic model visibility.

acceptance_cases.setup: Finalize an Agreement candidate without the adoption action required by the chosen approval policy.
acceptance_cases.expected: Candidate finalization and adoption are distinct. Build authority requires a separate adoption receipt naming the exact eligible Agreement identity/digest; the receipt may be recorded by an explicitly authorized combined user command.

acceptance_cases.setup: Register an externally prepared implementation against one exact Agreement and starting baseline.
acceptance_cases.expected: The handoff names that authority and actual resulting commit/tree. It does not claim Orchestrate performed the build.

acceptance_cases.setup: Present a dirty checkout while identifying only HEAD as the exact implementation.
acceptance_cases.expected: Register only the selected committed target and state prominently that dirty/untracked changes are excluded. Do not clean, commit, or certify those changes. A missing or unsupported committed target is refused.

acceptance_cases.setup: Supply a nonexistent commit, another repo's identity, or an implementation built from a mismatched authority.
acceptance_cases.expected: Nonexistent commit, wrong registered project, wrong authority, or contradicted source identity is rejected. Unobserved external build history is an attributed declaration, not a mechanically proven fact. Content alone cannot prove historical intent.

acceptance_cases.setup: Publish Agreement v2 after registering a build against v1.
acceptance_cases.expected: The historical build remains bound to v1 and its applicability to v2 is not assumed. No rewrite of prior records.

acceptance_cases.setup: Worker prose says complete while required handoff/evidence fields are absent or the operation is partial.
acceptance_cases.expected: It remains a claim/partial outcome, not successful build finalization or Audit acceptance.

acceptance_cases.setup: Exercise the boundary without Taskledger, Flow, task routing, checkpoints, or a scheduler installed.
acceptance_cases.expected: Discovery/Consensus/Audit and external target registration remain usable. Real Build execution is reported as deferred.

acceptance_cases.setup: Audit the known-good fixture against its matching Agreement with required checks available.
acceptance_cases.expected: The scripted path and live evaluator can return supported conformance. An always-blocking system fails this case.

acceptance_cases.setup: Audit a known required-behavior violation with a reproducible check.
acceptance_cases.expected: Identify the relevant requirement, concrete evidence, consequence and bounded correction; do not certify the implementation.

acceptance_cases.setup: A required runtime observation is missing.
acceptance_cases.expected: Report unverified behavior, not fabricated success and not an unsupported claim that the code is defective.

acceptance_cases.setup: A required check cannot run because the fixture environment is unavailable or misconfigured.
acceptance_cases.expected: The infrastructure limitation is distinguished from an assertion failure demonstrating nonconformance. The harness itself is checked before blaming the implementation.

acceptance_cases.setup: Request audit of commit A, then move HEAD to B during the run.
acceptance_cases.expected: The actual inspected/tested target stays A; final record and receipts identify A, not whatever HEAD means later.

acceptance_cases.setup: Supply a legitimate-looking passing receipt from another commit, environment, command, or Agreement.
acceptance_cases.expected: It cannot satisfy the current required observation without explicit established applicability. No automatic retargeting.

acceptance_cases.setup: Required checks pass, but an additional focused probe demonstrates a violation.
acceptance_cases.expected: The violation is retained; the number of passing checks does not override it.

acceptance_cases.setup: **Conditional: multiple assessments.** One assessor demonstrates a violation; others report no issue.
acceptance_cases.expected: Aggregation does not suppress the counterexample by majority vote. No mandatory committee is introduced by this case.

acceptance_cases.setup: Audit discovers a contradiction or consequential ambiguity in the Agreement.
acceptance_cases.expected: It records an authority issue; does not silently rewrite the Agreement, choose a new product rule, or start upstream work.

acceptance_cases.setup: Correct the known defect; retain an optional hardening suggestion unrelated to required behavior.
acceptance_cases.expected: The correction can close and conformance can pass. Optional advice does not become an endless acceptance blocker.

acceptance_cases.setup: Correct one defect but introduce another required-behavior regression.
acceptance_cases.expected: The new target does not inherit the old pass or close solely because the original finding was fixed.

acceptance_cases.setup: Run checks that create caches/temp files; attempt an edit to product code or the Agreement.
acceptance_cases.expected: Checks run in owned scratch; the target/authority remain unchanged. Forbidden writes are denied where claimed, otherwise detected and the affected verdict cannot be trusted.

acceptance_cases.setup: Edit one byte of each finalized artifact component separately, including a condition or parent reference.
acceptance_cases.expected: Required integrity verification detects the modification; no stale success is reused. Independently compute expected digests from retained bytes.

acceptance_cases.setup: Remove a component, truncate a manifest, change its schema version, or add duplicate required keys.
acceptance_cases.expected: A clear structural/integrity error; no silent defaulting of missing authoritative fields. Unknown future formats are not treated as current ones.

acceptance_cases.setup: Supply a final-looking Markdown file without a successfully published finalization record.
acceptance_cases.expected: Mere file existence does not establish finalized public output.

acceptance_cases.setup: Inspect, list lineage, and rerun a read-only check repeatedly.
acceptance_cases.expected: Finalized bytes/identity remain unchanged; no hidden model work or reinterpretation.

acceptance_cases.setup: Delete or corrupt the optional global index, then rebuild it.
acceptance_cases.expected: The same complete retained lineage can be reconstructed from authoritative manifests. Missing parents remain missing, not invented.

acceptance_cases.setup: Inject cyclic, cross-effort, dangling, or conflicting parent references.
acceptance_cases.expected: The lineage validator reports the actual structural problem; traversal terminates and does not select a plausible alternative.

acceptance_cases.setup: Read a bundle while another process finalizes it.
acceptance_cases.expected: Reader sees an incomplete state or a complete valid final artifact, never a mixture advertised as complete.

acceptance_cases.setup: Race two finalizers for one logical output.
acceptance_cases.expected: No torn or conflicting successful publications. Identical retries follow declared idempotency; different payloads cannot silently overwrite each other.

acceptance_cases.setup: Produce v2 after a build/audit referenced v1.
acceptance_cases.expected: The earlier records remain historically true; status does not relabel them as having used v2.

acceptance_cases.setup: Same bytes are serialized/reordered under supported encoding rules; use known hash vectors.
acceptance_cases.expected: Identity follows the declared byte/canonicalization contract consistently. Test fixed vectors as well as round-trips, so producer and consumer cannot share a hidden encoding bug.

acceptance_cases.setup: Keep only finalized public artifacts and required exact-target material; remove upstream run internals.
acceptance_cases.expected: Downstream phases still operate through the intended contract. Missing material genuinely required by the public contract is reported precisely.

acceptance_cases.setup: Kill the CLI during run creation or initial request capture.
acceptance_cases.expected: Restart reports incomplete/failed state or a valid committed operation; no phantom completed run.

acceptance_cases.setup: Fail a temporary artifact write or rename immediately before final publication.
acceptance_cases.expected: No consumer sees a successful incomplete artifact; prior valid state remains inspectable.

acceptance_cases.setup: Kill after all output bytes are written but before the finalization boundary.
acceptance_cases.expected: Files alone do not authorize downstream consumption. Recovery follows the documented incomplete-state path.

acceptance_cases.setup: Kill after finalization commits but before the caller receives success.
acceptance_cases.expected: Retry/recovery discovers the committed result; no duplicate conflicting publication or extra semantic work merely because acknowledgement was lost.

acceptance_cases.setup: Provider/check process starts; controller dies before recording its outcome.
acceptance_cases.expected: External outcome is unknown unless independently recovered. No automatic replay that assumes the effect never occurred.

acceptance_cases.setup: Cancel a long-running operation normally; then force-kill a separate trial.
acceptance_cases.expected: Terminal/cancellation records accurately distinguish the paths; confirmed evidence remains retained; ordinary graceful cleanup is not mistaken for crash qualification.

acceptance_cases.setup: Child hangs, ignores normal termination, or leaves a descendant running.
acceptance_cases.expected: Enforce the declared supported termination/cleanup contract with bounded waits. Any unproven descendant cleanup is surfaced, not claimed complete; unrelated processes are never targeted.

acceptance_cases.setup: Retry the same logical mutation with identical payload, then with a different payload and reused identity.
acceptance_cases.expected: Identical retry does not duplicate effects; conflicting reuse receives a clear error under the selected operation policy.

acceptance_cases.setup: A stale result arrives after cancellation, expiry, or a newer attempt.
acceptance_cases.expected: It cannot silently finalize the current attempt or overwrite newer authority. Preserve the late result as diagnostic material where appropriate.

acceptance_cases.setup: Simulate write failure, permissions failure, or unavailable artifact storage during recovery itself.
acceptance_cases.expected: The second failure is retained honestly; no false successful recovery or loss of the last trustworthy artifact.

acceptance_cases.setup: Race operations in independent runs and independent efforts; attempt concurrent operations on the same active run.
acceptance_cases.expected: Independent local operations cannot corrupt shared records. Same-run conflicting writes serialize or reject. Parallel model dispatch is optional, but any unsupported request for it is rejected before launch and before scratch sharing.

acceptance_cases.setup: Generate sequences of valid and invalid lifecycle actions and restart points.
acceptance_cases.expected: Public observations agree with a separately written minimal reference state model. Persist/shrink failures; add separate barriers-based tests for actual concurrent execution.

acceptance_cases.setup: Correct provider response, emitted through the real subprocess/protocol parser.
acceptance_cases.expected: Only validated data reaches the normal finalizer. The emulator does not write the final bundle or bypass production operations.

acceptance_cases.setup: Empty, truncated, malformed, oversized, wrong-schema, or unexpected-tool response.
acceptance_cases.expected: Bounded diagnostic and no falsely accepted result. Any allowed repair attempt is explicit in policy and counts.

acceptance_cases.setup: Emit events fragmented across reads, duplicated, reordered where invalid, or attributed to another invocation.
acceptance_cases.expected: Parser/state association is correct; duplicate output is not another vote/completion. Invalid ordering fails safely without a hang.

acceptance_cases.setup: Authentication failure, unavailable provider executable, capability mismatch, nonzero exit, or early EOF.
acceptance_cases.expected: Errors are classified; no silent provider/model substitution and no model-confidence report pretending the task completed.

acceptance_cases.setup: Exceed configured calls, output bytes, diagnostic size, or time limit.
acceptance_cases.expected: The declared bound is enforced at its actual control point. A soft admission budget is not advertised as a hard cap on already-running provider usage.

acceptance_cases.setup: Provider/check prints success while returning a failure; returns zero with no result; emits relevant errors to stderr.
acceptance_cases.expected: The engine retains all relevant observations and uses documented completion rules, not reassuring text or exit zero alone. Semantic proof still requires appropriate evidence.

acceptance_cases.setup: Process input includes shell metacharacters, quotes, spaces, and Unicode.
acceptance_cases.expected: Values are passed as intended arguments/data; no shell interpolation or altered target identity.

acceptance_cases.setup: Attempt to run an unapproved/destructive/live-service check described in model prose.
acceptance_cases.expected: The approved execution boundary is enforced. A prose suggestion is not authority to mutate production or run arbitrary extra commands.

acceptance_cases.setup: Provide credentials/config for the live adapter and inject secret sentinels into environment and stderr.
acceptance_cases.expected: Authorized authentication works without credentials leaking into prompts/artifacts/normal diagnostics; retained sensitive evidence follows explicit policy.

acceptance_cases.setup: Configure a three-attempt validation-repair allowance; reject two payloads and then return a valid payload. Repeat with allowance exhausted. Also test the one-attempt default.
acceptance_cases.expected: The predeclared allowance is enforced, attempts and feedback are retained, no valid semantic answer is retried to improve confidence, and exhausted attempts cannot fabricate finalization.

acceptance_cases.setup: A run is operated in Cursor while a configured managed role executes on a different provider/model.
acceptance_cases.expected: Host, execution provider, model and effort are distinct, attributable fields. The human-facing source label does not falsely imply execution identity.

acceptance_cases.setup: Host does not expose the actual model or reasoning setting; the operator supplies a value instead.
acceptance_cases.expected: Unknown actual metadata remains unknown; declared/reported settings are not promoted to observed facts.

acceptance_cases.setup: Compare manifest and generated frontmatter for host/model/effort, baseline, run ID, timestamps, and guide identity.
acceptance_cases.expected: They agree because presentation derives from recorded provenance. No need for manual frontmatter repair and no generic “run 1” as the only identifying information.

acceptance_cases.setup: Return valid inconclusive consensus, blocked verification, malformed output, and transport failure.
acceptance_cases.expected: Reports distinguish semantic result from operational state. “Command completed” does not mean Agreement adopted or implementation conforming.

acceptance_cases.setup: Fail halfway through a trial and inspect the test report.
acceptance_cases.expected: Retain fixture identity, actual commands/inputs, relevant outputs, observed state, and failure classification. Do not store only “assertion failed.”

acceptance_cases.setup: Test report contains missing/filtered/skipped lanes, unknown usage, or deferred Build.
acceptance_cases.expected: No claim of complete qualification. Unknown token/cost fields are not zero; cached/input/output/effort are not casually added into a fabricated billing number.

acceptance_cases.setup: A fixture consumer tries to import a producer's private application/storage internals.
acceptance_cases.expected: Compilation fails for the prohibited access. Public artifact consumers still compile and work.

acceptance_cases.setup: Add a forbidden dependency, alias, feature-gated edge, or re-export between phase implementations.
acceptance_cases.expected: The dependency-policy check fails. Crates alone do not prevent someone editing Cargo.toml to create a new dependency.

acceptance_cases.setup: Exercise public contract parsing/validation without producer runtime or database initialized.
acceptance_cases.expected: Contract code does not need live producer internals or implicit state mutation.

acceptance_cases.setup: Deliberately corrupt shared encoding/path helpers; run consumer tests using fixed external vectors.
acceptance_cases.expected: Independent expected values catch common-mode failures that shared round-trip helpers could conceal.

acceptance_cases.setup: Build the release artifact, install elsewhere, and test guide/phase resources.
acceptance_cases.expected: Embedded/bundled resources match the actual product version; missing source files or different cwd do not break installed execution.

acceptance_cases.setup: Full valid chain: three scripted investigator runs -> Consensus -> Agreement -> external known-good implementation -> Audit.
acceptance_cases.expected: All production boundaries execute; lineage joins exact inputs/outputs; the result is useful and conforming; no unauthorized phase continuation.

acceptance_cases.setup: Same chain, but external Build intentionally leaves one Agreement requirement broken, then supplies a correction.
acceptance_cases.expected: First audit identifies the violation; second can pass; both exact targets and their history remain. This tests rejection and successful closure.

acceptance_cases.setup: Finalize against one baseline; attempt substitution of a newer source, different request, or different Agreement at each handoff.
acceptance_cases.expected: Each affected boundary catches the mismatch. A valid-looking later artifact does not repair an invalid earlier link automatically.

acceptance_cases.setup: Interrupt/restart at publication and external-effect checkpoints throughout the journey.
acceptance_cases.expected: No partial success, fabricated evidence, duplicate vote, or silently repeated uncertain operation; independently reconstructable history.

acceptance_cases.setup: Actual installed low-strength host performs the small Discovery task; real Consensus/Audit roles consume their permitted artifacts.
acceptance_cases.expected: Real guide/skill/provider flow succeeds with honest provenance. The external Build step remains explicitly external; repeat in each claimed host/surface.

acceptance_cases.setup: Repeat E2E-01 in two efforts with identical labels and overlapping timings; delete the optional index.
acceptance_cases.expected: No cross-effort contamination or retargeting; rebuilt status/lineage identifies both chains accurately.

acceptance_cases.setup: Run packaged-path/process/recovery cases natively on the user's macOS environment.
acceptance_cases.expected: No `/var` spelling workaround or assumed Linux equivalence; record OS, filesystem and tool versions actually tested.

acceptance_cases.setup: **Conditional: additional platforms.** Run the same declared contract on Linux/Windows when supported.
acceptance_cases.expected: Real execution rather than cross-compilation alone qualifies behavior. Unsupported cases remain visible and are not counted as passes.

acceptance_cases.setup: Empty/minimal, typical, at-limit, and over-limit artifacts, logs, file counts, and path sizes.
acceptance_cases.expected: Useful processing within declared limits; explicit bounded errors beyond them; no silent truncation of mandatory content.

acceptance_cases.setup: Many retained runs, rebuildable index absent, and multiple simultaneous readers.
acceptance_cases.expected: Correct status/lineage without unacceptable unbounded growth or inconsistent snapshots. Record actual resource use; choose thresholds from intended personal workload rather than arbitrary large-system targets.

acceptance_cases.setup: Disposable fixture has no network, unexpected ambient host configuration, or missing external test service.
acceptance_cases.expected: Offline lanes remain offline. Dependencies are explicit; environment failures are visible and do not become false product verdicts.

acceptance_cases.setup: All opinions omit one original user rule; then try hiding an additional single-opinion feature in narrative or latitude.
acceptance_cases.expected: The governing rule is accounted for with source authority, not fabricated votes. Omitted required behavior or an unbound extra prevents readiness. Build/Audit cannot use an inferior plan to override the Agreement.

acceptance_cases.setup: Run the ordinary supported user journey with only request, project, chosen phase, selectors and approval.
acceptance_cases.expected: The user does not create UUIDs, manipulate database rows, or hand-author JSON; generated IDs and focused errors remain available to the operator.

acceptance_cases.setup: Mark an opinion known contaminated after publication, attempt to count it, replace its cohort slot, and attempt to count both runs.
acceptance_cases.expected: A separate invalidation notice preserves history. Known-compromised input is not eligible as a clean slot. Explicit replacement does not change the fixed denominator or create an extra vote; actual isolation remains honestly labeled.

acceptance_cases.setup: A check script edits a candidate implementation or requests an outside/live-service operation; compare its passing result with the untouched target.
acceptance_cases.expected: The permitted runner enforces its boundary, or the affected safety claim is unqualified. Probe-modified code is never evidence that the original target passes. No production data or target repository is changed.

acceptance_cases.setup: Complete Discovery -> Consensus -> adoption -> external registration -> Audit for a request already satisfied at the baseline.
acceptance_cases.expected: The same original commit is a valid target. No artificial requirement, code edit, or new product commit is necessary. The audit still checks the preservation/no-change contract and can pass.

acceptance_cases.setup: Supply a majority-backed proposal with an unresolved concrete counterexample, then a similar proposal with only non-material dissent.
acceptance_cases.expected: Both endorsement counts are accurate. The first is non-adoptable until narrowed/resolved from permitted evidence; the second can yield an eligible contested-majority package. No new research is silently run.

acceptance_cases.setup: Finalize G1, attempt downstream authority use before adoption, adopt G1, alter bytes, and attempt to reuse adoption for G2.
acceptance_cases.expected: Unadopted, ineligible, altered, or wrong-version authority is refused. Adoption is a separate exact-reference receipt; no forced consensus override exists.

acceptance_cases.setup: Adopt a conditional Agreement, then try to mark its prerequisite satisfied or not applicable without evidence.
acceptance_cases.expected: The condition remains attached to the affected obligations. Adoption is not evidence of condition satisfaction. No dependent completion or Audit PASS is granted without appropriate support or genuine non-applicability.

acceptance_cases.setup: Register externally authored code with claimed model, baseline, and test history that the application did not observe.
acceptance_cases.expected: Exact target and declared authority are checked, but historical authorship/production claims remain declared. No misleading statement that Orchestrate built or observed the preparation appears.

acceptance_cases.setup: Return a reassuring audit statement with one missing coverage row; use a fresh assessor and repeat with a substantiated defect plus an authority blocker.
acceptance_cases.expected: The missing row prevents PASS. The fresh assessment cannot be replaced by worker self-review. A proven defect yields CHANGES_REQUIRED with authority/evidence blockers retained; a failed invocation has no verdict.

acceptance_cases.setup: Deliberately break a critical guard, filter a required test to zero executions, and run known-good/known-bad grader controls.
acceptance_cases.expected: Independent controls catch the fault. Zero/filtered/skipped work cannot qualify a lane. All trial outcomes, supported surfaces, deferred capabilities, and NOT_EXECUTED results remain visible.
